rules.rationale: Android 16 preserves the final A13 managed-su implementation: signed OTA whitelist handling, package and command-line authorization, developer-mode hcall, denial reporting and the report daemon. Common implementation files are byte-identical or differ only by whitespace/line endings, except resolve_in_allowed_dirs uses an unsized array parameter to satisfy current Clang while preserving PATH_MAX behavior. The A13 unsafe-code removal remains present in the final source.
rules.necessity: Required to expose root only under the host-managed developer and signed-whitelist policy and to retain denied-request telemetry.
rules.performance: Authorization performs package lookup, whitelist parsing, signature hashing and hcall work only when su is invoked. Denial reporting uses a local datagram and does not block on cloud upload, but verbose warning logs and fallback package scans can add cost during repeated denied calls.
rules.security: High-privilege surface. Public-key verification, whitelist update ownership, command canonicalization, package-to-UID resolution and fail-closed behavior are security-critical. The report payload contains command, package, cwd and signature metadata and must remain protected by socket/SELinux policy.
validation_evidence: A13 and Android-16 final su implementations were compared file by file; headers, utilities, daemon and rc are identical, and remaining source differences are formatting plus the current-compiler array declaration adaptation.

Android-16 commit 2e0a75a42df3f785c500711ddada805d70e07ff2 changes only the managed su module and carries the complete final source set. Target build and runtime authorization oracles remain part of the final regression gate.

rules.rationale: The legacy su executable restored by A13 is present in Android 16 and is extended by the later authoritative managed-whitelist implementation rather than replaced by the unrelated upstream C++ su helper.
rules.necessity: Required as the executable entry point for the final BlueStacks root policy.
rules.performance: No persistent cost; the binary runs only on an explicit su request.
rules.security: The legacy unrestricted behavior must never bypass the later managed authorization path. Final source inspection confirms the whitelist/developer-mode checks are integrated before privilege execution.
validation_evidence: Android-16 tracks both upstream su.cpp and the BlueStacks su.c target, and the Soong su binary is built from the managed su.c source set.

rules.rationale: A13 selected TARGET_OUT_OPTIONAL_EXECUTABLES in Android.mk. Android 16 has no module-local Android.mk and expresses the same /system/xbin installation contract with install_in_xbin: true in Android.bp. The Soong target also carries every A13 source, HD static dependency, crypto/log dependency and report-daemon rc declaration.
rules.necessity: Required because callers and root tooling expect /system/xbin/su.
rules.performance: Build-system-only mapping with no runtime cost.
rules.security: Installation location does not grant privilege by itself; file mode, ownership, SELinux domain and managed authorization still require runtime verification.
validation_evidence: A13 Android.mk and Android-16 Android.bp were compared field by field; install_in_xbin is present and all functional sources and dependencies are represented.
